modules.name: cordic_sincos

ports.name: protocol_error_o
ports.description: One-clock pulse when start is asserted while busy

behavior: Reduce the unsigned 18-bit full-turn phase into the first quadrant and retain sine/cosine output signs.
Load the 36-bit Q4.32 X register with the quantized inverse CORDIC gain and perform exactly 18 shift-add micro-rotations.
Round the final Q4.32 values to signed Q2.30 using nearest rounding with half values away from zero.
Assert done_o 19 rising-edge intervals after an accepted start_i and hold results until the next completion.
constraints: Synthesizable Verilog-2001 without vendor CORDIC IP or DSP multiplication.
A request is accepted only in the idle state.
The angle lookup table uses the 18 constants frozen by the T02 bit-exact model.
corner_cases: Quadrant boundaries 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees follow the same iterative path as all other phases.
A repeated start while busy emits protocol_error_o and does not alter the active operation.
done_o and protocol_error_o are independent single-clock pulses.
verification_cases: Match all 74 T02 bit-exact vectors including cardinal angles, quadrant boundaries, 359 degrees and deterministic random angles.
Confirm a busy-time start request produces one error pulse without changing the result.

timing_diagrams.title: One iterative CORDIC operation
timing_diagrams.description: An idle start loads the reduced phase, busy covers 18 micro-rotations, and done publishes the rounded result.
